AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 6, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685
DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32
OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a):
  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles
  County Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Numbers 8056-015-014, 8056-015-016, and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Michael F G Trust; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8056-015-007 Negotiating parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City
  Manager; and Richard and Lillian Sneed, Norwalk Records; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Properties: Various remnant parcels along the I-5 freeway located within the City; Agency

  V.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8056-016-139; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Knights of Columbus; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of

  VI. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE § 54956.9(d)(2) – Significant Exposure to Litigation in one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Mayor Perez

FLAG SALUTE
  Councilmember Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel
 SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS – None.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Senior Center Independence Day Drive-Through Barbeque Recap.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of June 8,
  15, and 22, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll periods of May 16, 2021 - May 29,
  2021, in the total amount of $874,876.27; and May 30, 2021 – June 12, 2021 in the total amount of
  $1,243,287.54. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period June
  10, 2021 through June 30, 2021, in the total amount of $3,886,193.08. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – JUNE 23, 2021 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-42 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – CITY CLERK AND
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENTS - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution
  No. 21-42, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING
  THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENTS. 870-02

  Report

  7.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT – BUCKNAM AND ASSOCIATES - UTILITIES PROGRAM
  MANAGEMENT AND UTILITIES ENGINEERING SUPPORT SERVICES - Staff recommends City
  Council approve the agreement with Bucknam and Associates to provide Utilities Program
  Management and Utilities Engineering Support Services in the amount of $60,400; and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget,
  on behalf of the City in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1070-05

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENT – SAFE, CLEAN WATER PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council approve the
  Transfer agreement with the Los Angeles Flood Control District — Safe, Clean Water Program for
  Municipal Program Funds; and authorize the City Manager to execute the Transfer Agreement and any
  amendments, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1040-06

  Report

  9.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-43 – CHILD CARE SERVICES CONTRACTS – Staff recommends City Council:
   a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-43, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING CHILD CARE CONTRACT AGREEMENTS WITH THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF SOCIAL SERVICES FOR FUNDING OF THE CalWORKs Stage 2, 3, AND
  ALTERNATIVE PAYMENT CHILD CARE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2021/2022; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute the contracts and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City Attorney. 425-01

  Report

10. RESOLUTION NO. 21-44 – APPROVING AGREEMENTS FOR THE NORWALK SENIOR CENTER
  NUTRITION PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021/22– Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-44, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING AGREEMENTS WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT
  OF WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AGING AND COMMUNITY SERVICES, AND BETTER 4
  YOU MEALS CATERER FOR THE ELDERLY NUTRITION PROGRAM FISCAL YEAR 2021/22;
  and

  b.  approve amendment No. 5 with the Los Angeles County Workforce Development, Aging and
  Community Services to fund the Elderly Nutrition Program in the amount of $690,100, from July 1,
  2021 through June 30, 2022; and

  c.  approve an agreement with Better 4 You Meals Food Service to provide cooked meals for the
  Elderly Nutrition Program in the amount of $602,610, from July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022;
  and

  d.  authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment and agreement, and any amendments,
  provided funds are available in the budget, on behalf of the City, in forms approved by the City
  Attorney.
  425-02-03

  Report

11. RESOLUTION NOS. 21-46 AND 21-47 – APPROVING AND ACCEPTING THE NEGOTIATED
  EXCHANGE OF PROPERTY TAX REVENUES RESULTING FROM THE ANNEXATIONS OF TRACT
  NO. 82127 TO THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES LIGHTING MAINTENANCE DISTRICT 10045A AND
  PROJECT L 108-2019 TO THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES LIGHTING MAINTENANCE DISTRICT
  NO. 1687 – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 21-46, A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF THE
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE LITTLE LAKE CEMETERY
  DISTRICT, THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES OF THE GREATER LOS ANGELES COUNTY VECTOR
  CONTROL DISTRICT, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COUNTY SANITATION DISTRICT
  NO. 18 OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LA MIRADA, THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LA MIRADA AS SUCCESSOR OF INTEREST TO THE LA
  MIRADA SOUTHEAST RECREATION AND PARK DISTRICT, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK AS SUCCESSOR OF INTEREST TO THE NORWALK–SOUTHEAST
  RECREATION AND PARK DISTRICT, AND THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE WATER
  REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA APPROVING AND ACCEPTING
  THE NEGOTIATED EXCHANGE OF PROPERTY TAX REVENUES RESULTING FROM
  ANNEXATION OF TRACT NO. 82127 TO COUNTY LIGHTING MAINTENANCE DISTRICT
  10045A; and

  b.  Resolution No. 21-47, A JOINT RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF THE
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES OF THE GREATER LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY VECTOR CONTROL DISTRICT, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COUNTY
  SANITATION DISTRICT NO. 18 OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF LA MIRADA AS SUCCESSOR OF INTEREST TO THE LA MIRADA SOUTHEAST
  RECREATION AND PARK DISTRICT, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AS
  SUCCESSOR OF INTEREST TO THE NORWALK–SOUTHEAST RECREATION AND PARK
  DISTRICT, AND THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT
   OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA APPROVING AND ACCEPTING THE NEGOTIATED EXCHANGE
  OF PROPERTY TAX REVENUES RESULTING FROM ANNEXATION OF L 108-2019 TO
  COUNTY LIGHTING MAINTENANCE DISTRICT 1687. 638-08

  Report

  12. AGREEMENT - HOMELESS PREVENTION AND RAPID REHOUSING SERVICES - Staff
  recommends City Council approve an agreement with Kingdom Causes Bellflower for homeless
  prevention and rapid rehousing services in the amount of $75,000 per year, for a two-year term of July
  1, 2021 through June 30, 2023 allowing for two 1-year extensions; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the agreement, and any amendments, provided there Is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 315-10

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  13. ADVISORY BODIES - Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

RESOLUTIONS

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 21-45 – INTENTION TO CONSIDER GRANTING A PUBLIC UTILITY PIPELINE
  FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE PIPELINE COMPANY, LLC. – Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 21-45, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO GRANT A PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO TORRANCE PIPELINE
  COMPANY, LLC; and schedule a public hearing for August 3, 2021. 618-03

  Report

REPORTS

  15. ADOPTION OF HEART OF NORWALK PLAN - Staff recommends City Council adopt the Heart of
  Norwalk Vision Plan. 1405-06

  Report

  16. FIXED ROUTE BUS SERVICES - RESUMPTION OF FRONT DOOR BOARDING AND FARE
  COLLECTION - Staff recommends City Council receive and file. 1120-05

  Report

  17. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – JULY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive and
  file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 2, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
